title: Ten pull_request runs sit queued since Nov 11 on two old branches; find why they never started and cancel the dead ones
why: Coordinator 05:08 CST Nov 14 (REST total_count 10, all pull_request, created 2026-11-11 20:21 to 20:50Z; none started in about 2 days) and triage's own REST read at 05:08 CST (actions list_workflow_runs, status queued, total_count 10): checks runs 43095529627 (workflow checks 8314), 43097100885 (8315), 43097831985 (8316), 43098118148 (8317), 43098335788 (8318) and lane-touched-tests runs 43095529619 (2102), 43097100920 (2103), 43097831996 (2104), 43098118159 (2105), 43098335794 (2106). Two branches: glossary-records-half (head 0e41a456, one pair) and fix-check-after-main-merge (heads 408ea7a0, 517bad5a, cb576416, a4399310; four pairs). They look stuck or superseded, not a live wait. NOT read: whether those PRs are open or closed, why they never started (a runner label, a concurrency group, an expired queue), and what a stuck queued run costs. The coordinator did not decide whether to cancel; a cancel is a write on CI, so it needs a session that may do it and the owner's standing grant for the act (acts the cloud refuses: a cancel is not on that list). Check idea (unbuilt): a sweep that lists queued runs older than a set age whose PR is closed or whose head moved, and names them; any watcher states its cost first (process starts, files written, how often) and reads on demand inside a running process. Update 05:10 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 05:10, REST 05:09, relayed; not re-read by triage): the queued heads sit on PRs #2563 and #2597, both merged 2026-11-12T01:42:23Z, so they are not live. Run 43098335794 (lane-touched-tests) reads queued. Still not read: why they never started, and the cost of a stuck run. The coordinator will not start a lane and says a cancel is outside its standing grants (only branch protection and branch delete are named). Triage's read, labelled as a read and not a grant: cancelling a queued run on a merged PR loses nothing and a cancelled run can be run again, so it is not an act that cannot be undone; but no session holds a grant that names it, so the batch runner (which merges and owns CI upkeep) or the owner names the session first. Triage cancels nothing. Pick 05:11 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 05:12, its own, labelled): runner 10 cancels the ten queued runs. The coordinator read PRs #2563 and #2597 merged by REST at 05:10, and that the runs show pull_requests empty. No owner item. If the tool or the classifier refuses, runner 10 stops and the coordinator tells triage; then the owner item is triage's to post. The two causes (why they never started, the cost of a stuck run) stay unread. RESULT 05:12 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 05:13, relayed from runner 10; triage did not run it): runner 10 tried the cancel on all ten runs (43098335794, 43098335788, 43098118148, 43098118159, 43097831996, 43097831985, 43097100920, 43097100885, 43095529619, 43095529627). GitHub refused each with 409 "Cannot cancel a workflow run that has not been queued yet"; nothing changed, no retry. The runs read `queued` by REST but GitHub treats them as not yet queued. Age: about 2.5 days at 05:13 CST by created_at (the coordinator's arithmetic from the stamps; runner 10's "about 9 h" was wrong). Left: a web UI cancel, or a delete of the runs; a delete cannot be undone, so it is not for a session. Not read and not tried: GitHub's force-cancel endpoint for runs that will not cancel. Harm of leaving them: UNMEASURED (no live run waits on them; runner 11 read them as no live wait). Coordinator's pick: leave them. Triage's call: no owner item now, since no harm is shown; reopen as an owner yes/no (web UI cancel or delete) if a run ever blocks a live PR or the queue count matters.
